patch_description: This version implements a shared-trunk routing strategy: (1) destinations are processed in a greedy "expensive-first" order so that costly destinations get to choose their paths first and cheap destinations can then piggyback on the already-used shared edges; (2) for each destination, k-shortest candidate paths are scored against a set of `shared_edges` already emitted by earlier destinations, where reuse of shared edges counts as free (never a discount, only full reuse), strongly biasing later routes onto a common trunk; (3) a one-step lookahead is applied: candidates for remaining destinations are pre-scored against a hypothetical future trunk (current shared edges plus edges used by other already-scored candidates), so the router prefers edges that multiple other destinations will also want, forming a shared backbone early. Baseline Dijkstra paths are always included as candidates, guaranteeing valid fallbacks and no regressions versus the naive algorithm.
